Here is the outcome list for staging the project. I'll write no roadmap text until you've ranked it.

**Roadmap file:** `specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md`. The skill names it from the spec's filename, so there is no name to choose.

## Outcomes (unranked)

The candidates come from the spec's R1–R11 and the sections those rulings point to. I've folded R5 (shared code) and R11 (defaults are configuration) into the choices below, since they constrain how things are built rather than what you get.

| # | Outcome | From | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Catalog rows in Parquet for one real archived quarter, parsed from SEC `master.idx`, with the original bytes kept alongside | R1, R3, R6; §4.4–4.6 | Small: probably tens of MB and a handful of requests per recent quarter. This is from memory, not checked; one quarter's `index.json` listing would confirm it. |
| O2 | A historical baseline over a quarter range you choose, with every quarter either published or listed as a gap | R1; §4.2 Backfill | Depends on the range, which the spec leaves open. Requests are trivial (a few files per quarter at 3 req/s). Data volume is roughly the O1 size times the number of quarters. Older quarters may need extra legacy-format fixtures (§4.6). |
| O3 | Daily indexes added on an ongoing basis, catching up after missed runs and across quarter boundaries | R2; §4.2 Daily | About 250 small files a year, so cheap. The cost is mostly correctness work: overlap, dedup and pending sources. |
| O4 | Rebuilding the catalog from stored raw bytes after a parser change, with no SEC requests | R6 | Local compute only; the core stage measures it. |
| O5 | Readers get a whole quarter through one active pointer and manifest, never partial files | R9; §4.6 | Code only. |
| O6 | A weekly re-read of quarterly indexes that records additions and changes, and removes filings only after you approve a specific source hash | R7, R10; §4.4 | One full re-download of the supported range per run (same volume as O2), plus your time to approve each closed-quarter withdrawal. |
| O7 | All SEC traffic goes through one shared budget (3 req/s, identifying User-Agent), however many workers run | R8, R11; §4.3 | Code only. Only running it shows whether the throughput is enough. |
| O8 | The pipeline runs unattended on Azure: ADF schedules, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, managed identities | R4; §4.1, §4.9 | Azure spend can't be estimated yet, because the spec leaves resource sizes and region to deployment (§4.8). Measured by the track's core stage. |
| O9 | Operations you can rely on: run reports, alerts, runbooks, and an exercised rollback | §4.7, §7–8 | Mostly your time, plus Log Analytics ingestion (unknown until it runs). |

## Proposed tracks

- **Track A: Filing-index catalog** (O1–O7). I propose this as a known progression, because the spec fixes the contracts from parsing through reconciliation.
- **Track B: Azure operation** (O8–O9). I also propose this as a known progression.
- **Why split them:** the catalog stands without Azure, since it runs and is testable locally. The ADR choosing Azure is still *Proposed*, not accepted. Joining the tracks would make the catalog wait on that decision and on Azure setup. Track B does consume Track A's CLI, so it can't finish first, but its core stage doesn't need all of A.

If you see part of A as open rather than known, say so and I'll mark it research. Reconciliation (O6) is the likeliest candidate, because the withdrawal policy is new in this draft.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 in a uv workspace, from `.python-version` and `pyproject.toml`.
- The spec puts all code in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest`. The scaffold also has `sec-edgar-client`, `-download` and `-index-ingest`, which the spec doesn't mention. Should those stay out of scope, or is the split intended?
- Backfill, daily ingestion and reconciliation share one downloader, parser and publisher (R5).
- The numbers in §4.8 are starting configuration values, not guarantees (R11).
- Azure is the platform (R4), but the ADR and spec are still pending acceptance.

## Optional probe

With your OK, I could fetch one recent quarter's `full-index/<year>/QTR<n>/index.json` listing to firm up the O1 and O2 size notes. That is a single request with an identifying User-Agent.

**Your call:** please rank the outcomes within each track and the two tracks against each other. Also confirm or change the split and each track's kind, answer the package question, and say yes or no to the probe.
